Adyen refuses small clients, under the million :/
I wish Adyen was as good at marketing and hype as Stripe was. Stripe is really good at making themselves look like a way bigger deal than they are.
Are they still an XML heavy 'integration partner'? They were when I worked at a casino that used them.
Adyen ... I have only bad stories about them. I guess they totally deserve this.
Adyen is much more 'bare metal.' Think more like a modern Authorize.net. Nobody comes close to Stripe's turnkey developer-friendliness.

One of the bigger drawbacks of Adyen vs Stripe... they require a crazy reserve (in the millions) if your model is subscription based, to be able to refund all customers if you go bankrupt. Not one other PSP requires such a huge reserve, so we decided not to work with them.
Adyen is an 'interchange-plus' payment processor, which means they pass on the interchange fee charged to them by the payment networks, plus a fixed markup, unlike Stripe's flat 2.9%+30c rate.

Generally, Adyen is cheaper than Stripe but Stripe is easier to integrate. The more volume you process, the more a switch to Adyen makes sense; Adyen also has minimum monthly invoices when Stripe does not.

Longtime Stripe user did about a year-long stint with Adyen. Stripe beats Adyen on ease of integration, ease of using the back office, chargebacks, etc hands down. Adyen made us integrate with COM for card-present. After hundreds of hours invested, we ditched Adyen; their pricing wasn't any cheaper than Stripe with interchange plus.

I implemented Adyen for a company I was consulting for. I liked it. Their integration was not as terrible as many here make it seem. It allowed us to offer every payment option under the sun, including 'native' options like iDEAL for the Netherlands and Sofort-Überweisung for Germany.

Adyen's pricing model looks much more attractive on paper, but the integration complexity and minimum processing volumes usually keep early-stage startups on Stripe or Braintree despite the higher percentage fees.
